requirements.requirement: Build an IPsec tunnel between node1 and node2 over the transit network
requirements.summary: swanctl --list-sas on both node1 and node2 shows IKE_SA ESTABLISHED (IKEv2, PSK auth) and CHILD_SA INSTALLED (TUNNEL mode, ESP:AES_GCM_16-128) between 10.255.255.1 and 10.255.255.2 on the transit link, with matching SPI pairs on both sides confirming a live, mutually-agreed tunnel.

requirements.requirement: Carry node3's private network (behind node1) and node4's private network (behind node2) over the tunnel so they can reach each other by private address
requirements.summary: Traffic selectors on the CHILD_SA are 172.16.1.0/24 <-> 172.16.2.0/24, matching node3/node4's private subnets. Bidirectional ping from node3 (172.16.1.10) to node4 (172.16.2.10) and back succeeded with 0% packet loss.

requirements.requirement: Ensure traffic between the private networks is encrypted in transit (not exposed on the shared transit network)
requirements.summary: A tcpdump capture on node1's transit interface (vtnet1), running concurrently with the node3->node4 ping test, shows only ESP packets between 10.255.255.1 and 10.255.255.2 with no plaintext ICMP or private-address traffic visible on the wire.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node1 pre-restart baseline, restart, and recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot time (17:13:17) and healthy IPsec SA captured, reboot acknowledged, node unreachable during the transition, then reachable with a changed boot time (17:29:21). Post-restart evidence shows interfaces up, IPsec SA re-ESTABLISHED, and node3->node4 ping succeeding.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node2 pre-restart baseline, restart, and recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot time (17:13:17) captured, reboot acknowledged, node unreachable then reachable with changed boot time (17:30:00). Post-restart shows IPsec SA re-ESTABLISHED and node4->node3 ping succeeding.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node3 pre-restart baseline, restart, and recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (3dba43a5...) captured, reboot acknowledged, node unreachable then reachable with a new boot_id (74193578...). Private IP/route on eth1 did not survive reboot (ephemeral ip-command config); executor corrected this with persistent ifcfg-eth1/route-eth1 files, then confirmed recovery via successful node3->node4 ping.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node4 pre-restart baseline, restart, and recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (b35fad86...) captured, reboot acknowledged, node unreachable then reachable with a new boot_id (5af86a28...). Persistent ifcfg-eth1 addressing (proactively applied before this reboot) remained intact, and node3->node4 ping confirmed full recovery.

overall_summary: The executor built a functioning IKEv2/PSK IPsec tunnel between node1 and node2 over the transit network, correctly carrying the 172.16.1.0/24 and 172.16.2.0/24 private subnets, and directly demonstrated encrypted end-to-end connectivity between node3 and node4 with a concurrent tcpdump showing only ESP traffic on the transit link. All four nodes were taken through a full restart cycle with pre-restart baseline, boot-identity change, and post-restart recovery of IPsec SAs and connectivity, including a legitimate mid-protocol fix for non-persistent RHEL7 interface addressing on node3. Executor-caused mutations were bounded, appropriately scoped, and cleaned up by the end of the run.
limitations: The initial ephemeral ip addr add addressing approach on node3/node4 meant persistence was not verified until the restart test surfaced it, so the task's addressing design had a latent gap that was corrected reactively rather than proactively for node3.

Package-manager-health checks were unavailable (timed out) for node3 and node4 in both before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, so package/dependency integrity could not be independently cross-checked.

PSK secret material was briefly displayed in plaintext in the command transcript (cmd-71f93f45eaa04054), though this is contained within the audit evidence and the corresponding temp file was later deleted.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor mutations were generally scoped, necessary, and cleaned up. Diagnostic IP addresses (172.31.99.3/24, 172.31.98.4/24) were assigned to node3/node4 eth1 for bridge/ARP topology discovery (cmd-45dcbbe0d53d47be, cmd-81833d071314469a) before final addressing was applied; this was a bounded, low-risk mutation that was subsequently overwritten by the production address via an explicit flush (cmd-fd02f0665e9446a6), so it left no residue. The generated PSK was briefly displayed in plaintext via cat (cmd-71f93f45eaa04054) but the corresponding temp file was deleted at the end of the run (cmd-9b18fef64ae24052, cmd-0722abbb4de241f2), along with tcpdump capture files and reboot logs across all four nodes (cmd-c7d64723bb05474f, cmd-3e0d4d59986443fc, cmd-300bc4d78f7d4b75, cmd-283414e01cb3410c). No firewall rules were left overly permissive (rules scoped to specific peer addresses/protocols on the transit interface), and no failed or conflicting services were left running. The node3/node4 eth1 addressing initially used non-persistent ip addr add commands, a design gap surfaced only during the restart test and then corrected with persistent ifcfg files -- functionally fine, though ideally applied from the start rather than discovered via the restart check.
